mentions.name: Rover
mentions.description: Rover is a search engine for petabytes of raw logs in Azure that strips away the "indexing tax" that makes large-scale logging expensive. Instead of moving massive data to heavy compute nodes, the engine surgically fetches only the specific bytes needed to answer a query directly from storage. It shifts work from memory-hungry string parsing to hardware-accelerated bitwise math, scanning 1TB of data in about 1.2 seconds for roughly $0.01.
mentions.problem: Large-scale logging is expensive due to the indexing tax of moving massive amounts of data to heavy compute nodes.
mentions.audience: Teams and individuals dealing with large-scale log search and scaling challenges
mentions.source_excerpt: My friend and I are building Rover, a search engine for petabytes of raw logs in Azure: https://roverhq.io/ The core idea is to strip away the "indexing tax" that usually makes large-scale logging so expensive.
